sentences.text: ICAC’s 1996 community attitude survey sought to inform its prevention and education programs through the views of 511 randomly selected NSW adults.
sentences.support: The 1996 community attitude survey was conducted with a random sample of 511 people

sentences.text: It examined corruption perceptions, standards expected in public and private workplaces, reporting attitudes and support for ICAC.
sentences.support:
The survey explored people's general 
attitudes to corruption, particularly in relation to public and private sector workplaces.

sentences.text: ICAC reported that respondents judged public sector workplace behaviour more strictly than comparable behaviour in private business.
sentences.support:
Respondents regarded workplace behaviour in the public sector more stringently 
than workplace behaviour in private business.

sentences.text: ICAC reported that 90% felt responsible for reporting corruption, while 76% believed those who reported it would suffer.
sentences.support:
A very high percentage feel they have some 
responsibility to report corruption (90%)

findings.quote:
Respondents regarded workplace behaviour in the public sector more stringently 
than workplace behaviour in private business.

A very high percentage feel they have some 
responsibility to report corruption (90%), and that they know how serious corruption needs 
to be before reporting it (58%).

notes: Results describe community views, not measured corruption or verified reporting consequences. No numbered recommendations list.
